get.summary: Get Default Option for a Trading Opportunity
get.description: Checks whether the current account can use an option trading opportunity for the underlying stock and opportunity type, and returns the recommended default option contract. Use it to prefill the strategy preview when the Client opens an option trading opportunity from a position. The opportunity type and position direction determine the strategy: `1` (protection) maps to Protective Put for a long position and Protective Call for a short position; `2` (income) maps to Covered Call for a long position and Covered Put for a short position. When the account does not meet the conditions, the request fails; show the returned `message` to the Client and do not open the strategy page.

parameters.description: Underlying stock security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL`

Opportunity type:

- `1` - Protection (hedge the price risk of the position)
- `2` - Income (sell options to collect premium)

parameters.description: Direction of the stock position: pass `LONG` when the position quantity is greater than 0; otherwise pass `SHORT`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Default Option for a Trading Opportunity” operation.

get.description: Returns the expiration dates available for option strategy screening on the underlying stock. Use it for the expiration date picker on the option chain Strategies page. Pass the selected `expire_date` as `expire_date` to Search Option Strategy Recommendations. The option chain strategy feature on the market data side uses this endpoint as well.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Underlying stock security ID (counter_id), for example `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List Expiration Dates for Option Strategies” operation.

post.description: Returns recommended option strategies with probability of profit, maximum profit, and maximum loss, based on the Client’s outlook for the underlying stock (scenario), target price or price range, expiration date, and position. Use it for the result list on the option chain Strategies page. After the Client selects a result, prefill a single-leg or multi-leg option order with each leg’s `counter_id` and `order`. This endpoint only calculates recommendations and does not place orders. The option chain strategy feature on the market data side uses this endpoint as well.

scene.description:
Scenario:

- `1` - Expect the price to rise to the target
- `2` - Expect the price to fall to the target
- `3` - Expect a large move, at least to one boundary of the range
- `4` - Expect the price to stay within the range
- `5` - Holding the stock and hedging downside risk
- `6` - Holding the stock and collecting premium to improve returns

Scenarios `1`, `2`, `5`, and `6` require `price`; scenarios `3` and `4` require `up_price` and `down_price`.

price.description: Target price for single-target scenarios. Pass an empty string for other scenarios.

up_price.description: Upper bound of the price range for range scenarios. Pass an empty string for other scenarios.

down_price.description: Lower bound of the price range for range scenarios. Pass an empty string for other scenarios.

side.description:
Stock position:

- `0` - No position
- `1` - Long
- `2` - Short

hold_price.description: Average cost of the stock position. Pass it when `side` is `1` or `2`; pass an empty string when there is no position.

filter.description:
Filter by opening direction:

- `0` - All
- `1` - Sell
- `2` - Buy

sort_key.description:
Sort field:

- `0` - Probability of profit
- `1` - Maximum profit
- `2` - Maximum loss

size.description: Number of items per page. Fewer items than `size` means there are no more results.

post.summary: List Rights Issue and Tender Offer Events
post.description:
Lists, page by page, corporate action events that require an active subscription, such as rights issues and tender offers, for the target account. Used for the rights issue and tender offer list page. You can filter by market, event type, and subscription status.

An empty `order_id` or `"0"` means the Client has not subscribed yet. The Broker App shows the event details and `max_subscribe_quantity`; after the Client enters a quantity, call `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/calculate_fee` and then `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/apply`. A populated `order_id` means a subscription order already exists; use it to call `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/detail`.

Pagination: `page` starts from `1`. When `page × size` is greater than or equal to `data.total`, there is no more data. Specify the target account in the `x-target-aaid` request header.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target account. The operation returns or processes subscription data for this account.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List Rights Issue and Tender Offer Events” operation.

post.description:
Gets the details of a rights issue or tender offer subscription by order ID. Used on the subscription details page to show the applied quantity, distributed quantity, fee, and key dates. Get `order_id` from the event list or subscription history.

The Broker App decides which actions to offer from the response. Before the end of the day of `end_time`, and when `state` is not `REVOKED`, `UNDISTRIBUT`, or `DISTRIBUTED`, the Client can cancel through `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/reovke`. When `state` is `REVOKED` and the closing date has not passed, the Client can recalculate the fee with `choices_quantity` and subscribe again. The server makes the final decision. Specify the target account in the `x-target-aaid` request header.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target account. The operation returns or processes subscription data for this account.

order_id.description: Subscription order ID from `order_id` of the list or history, converted to a number

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Subscription Order Details” operation.

post.description:
Calculates the total fee for a subscription from the event and quantity. Used for confirmation before submission. Call it after the Client enters a quantity and selects submit; the Broker App shows the returned fee in the confirmation dialog, and calls `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/apply` after the Client confirms. Also call it before resubscribing to a cancelled order.

This operation only calculates the fee and does not create a subscription order. On failure, show `message` to the Client and do not submit the subscription. Specify the target account in the `x-target-aaid` request header.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target account. The operation returns or processes subscription data for this account.

ann_id.description: Corporate action event ID from `ann_id` of the event, converted to a number

quantity.description: Number of shares to subscribe, as a positive integer string. It cannot exceed `max_subscribe_quantity` of the event.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Calculate Subscription Fee” operation.

post.summary: Submit Rights Issue or Tender Offer Subscription
post.description:
Submits a subscription instruction for an event. For a rights issue, the Client subscribes to new shares at the rights issue price (an excess rights application when `is_excess` is `true`). For a tender offer, the quantity is the number of shares tendered at the offer price.

Prerequisite: call `POST /v1/portfolio/corpaction/subscribe/calculate_fee` first, show the total fee to the Client, and get confirmation. Success means only that the application was submitted, not that it is complete. Track progress through `state` in the subscription details or history. On failure, show `message` to the Client and confirm that the event is still open before deciding whether to retry. Specify the target account in the `x-target-aaid` request header.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target account. The operation returns or processes subscription data for this account.

ann_id.description: Corporate action event ID from `ann_id` of the event, converted to a number

quantity.description: Number of shares to subscribe, as a positive integer string. It cannot exceed `max_subscribe_quantity` of the event.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Rights Issue or Tender Offer Subscription” operation.

data.description: Always `null`. Use `code` to determine whether the request succeeded.

post.description:
Cancels a submitted rights issue or tender offer subscription order. Used for the “Withdraw Application” action on the subscription details page. The Broker App shows this action only before the end of the day of `end_time`, and when `state` is not `REVOKED`, `UNDISTRIBUT`, or `DISTRIBUTED`. The server makes the final decision.

The path segment `reovke` is the existing spelling. Do not change it to `revoke`. On success, query the subscription details again to refresh the status; a cancelled order can be resubmitted before the closing date. get.description:
Checks, by withdrawal scenario, whether the Client must complete a questionnaire first. The Broker App calls it at two points. Before the Client confirms a withdrawal, it checks `withdrawChangeBank` and `withdrawOversea` and passes the bank card, amount, and currency of this withdrawal so that the service can evaluate the withdrawal ratio condition and information changes. After the withdrawal request is submitted, the result page checks `withdrawHK` and `withdraw` and passes `is_all`.

When `result` is `true` and `hit_position` is returned, guide the Client to the questionnaire for `hit_position`. If this happens before withdrawal, pause the submission. When the pre-withdrawal check returns a `draft_id` greater than `0`, an unlinked questionnaire draft from the same day with the same withdrawal details already exists. Save the value and, after the withdrawal request succeeds, call `POST /v1/questionnaire/submit` to link the draft to the withdrawal request. Overwrite the saved value with each new check result, and clear it when `draft_id` is `0`.

After the Client completes the questionnaire, this operation may still return `result` as `true` for the same scenario, so the Broker App must remember that the questionnaire for this withdrawal has been handled to avoid guiding the Client again. If this operation fails, the Broker App does not block the withdrawal flow. The same operation also decides whether questionnaires apply in other scenarios, such as deposits.

- `withdrawChangeBank` - Bank card change questionnaire, checked before withdrawal. Precondition: the Client has at least 2 bound bank cards
- `withdrawOversea` - Overseas withdrawal questionnaire, checked before withdrawal. Precondition: the Client is located in Greater China and the receiving bank card is outside it
- `withdrawHK` - Hong Kong stock withdrawal questionnaire, checked after the withdrawal request is submitted
- `withdraw` - General withdrawal questionnaire, checked after the withdrawal request is submitted

Side effect: binds the questionnaire draft to the withdrawal request. `card_id`, `amount`, and `currency` must match the questionnaire draft, or the service rejects the link. Linking the same draft to the same withdrawal again does not create a new record, and linking it to a different withdrawal is rejected. Do not pass `findings` when linking; answers in the request are treated as a new questionnaire submission. Clear the saved `draft_id` whether the link succeeds or fails. A failure of this operation does not affect the submitted withdrawal request, and the Broker App does not block navigation to the result page.

The same operation is also used by the questionnaire page to submit answers. The additional fields that usage requires are outside the scope of this description.

The withdrawal and currency exchange pages also use this operation to read money market fund holdings and prompt the Client to redeem first.

post.summary: Validate Order Card (Hong Kong and Singapore)
post.description:
Validates the order parameters of an order card generated in an AI conversation (for Hong Kong and Singapore stock accounts). If validation passes, the service returns normalized order parameters that you can use to render the card and submit the order. If validation fails, use the business code to guide the Client through the prerequisite, such as opening an account, depositing funds, enabling options or crypto permissions, or verifying the trade password, and then validate again.

A validation result becomes stale when the password, funds, or permissions change. Validate again if the Client returns to the card after a long pause. Before placing the order, call `POST /v1/trade/widget/submit/check` to get the items the Client must confirm. Numeric fields in the request body can also be sent as strings. For US stock accounts, use `POST /v1/trade/us/widget/validate`.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`. If the trade password has not been verified, the operation returns business code `402000` so that you can guide the Client to verify it.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Validate Order Card (Hong Kong and Singapore)” operation.

400.description: The service rejected the request because a business rule or input validation failed. Review the business codes and correct the request before retrying.

The Client has not deposited funds. Guide the Client to deposit
Insufficient buying power. Guide the Client to deposit, then validate again
The account does not have options trading permission. Guide the Client to enable it, then validate again
The account does not have crypto trading permission. Guide the Client to enable it, then validate again
The trade password has not been verified or the trade token has expired. Ask the Client to verify the trade password, then validate again

post.description:
Before submitting the order of an order card (for Hong Kong and Singapore stock accounts), pass the normalized order parameters returned by `POST /v1/trade/widget/validate` to get the reminders, assessments, and declarations that the Client must confirm. If the list is empty, submit the order directly. Otherwise, show each item and obtain the Client's confirmation before submitting. This operation does not create an order.

For a declaration item (`type=3`) without `click_url`, sign the declaration after the Client selects the confirmation: if `flag` in `param` is `options_general_risk_disclaimer`, call `POST /v1/member/account/options/agree`; otherwise pass the value as `type` to `POST /v1/record/questionnaire`. After signing succeeds, call this operation again and submit the order only when no items remain.

Records the Client's confirmation of, or answers to, a trading declaration, risk notice, or questionnaire. Common cases: before an order, depending on the Client's risk level, show the “insist on trading” declaration (`spac_trade_declare`) or the “important notice” (`spac_trade_notice`) and, after the Client agrees, pass `items: {"agree": "true"}`; for the Hong Kong listed derivatives experience questionnaire (`derivatives.HK`), pass an option value such as `items: {"derivatives_exper": "one"}`; for a declaration item of an order card, pass `param.flag` as `type`. After the record succeeds, run the original check again before continuing with the order. If it fails, show `message` and do not continue with the order.

This operation is also used to report the derivatives knowledge questionnaire before an IPO subscription, to confirm risks before creating a recurring investment plan, and to submit investor assessments and professional investor certification questionnaires.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

post.description:
Modifies the price, quantity, or amount of an open stock order and can adjust the attached take-profit and stop-loss orders at the same time. It applies to regular orders and triggered conditional orders. Use `POST /v1/povs/replace` for conditional orders that have not been triggered, `POST /v1/tube/stock_contract/replace` for options orders, and `POST /v1/attached_order/replace` to modify only the attached orders. Omit `price` for market orders; the price of a limit-type order cannot be 0. A successful response means only that the modification request was accepted; check the final state through the order details or order push updates. On success, refresh the order list and assets. On failure, show `message`; the original order remains unchanged.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `replaceOrder`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

get.summary: Get Option Open Order Calculation Factors

Do not call this endpoint for non-margin-mode options or order amendment; for amendment, use Get Option Replace Order Calculation Factors.

The parameters are the same as Get Option Open Order Calculation Factors, plus the original order ID. The response also includes `single_option_im_margin`, calculated for the direction of the original order.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

Leg quantities are in shares: for an option leg, the combination quantity multiplied by `lot_size` returned by Get Multi-Leg Option Order Configuration; for a stock leg, the combination quantity multiplied by the leg's `ratio_quantity`. Do not call this endpoint when the price or quantity is 0.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

The result is a suggestion only: the card is redeemed only if you put `card_id` into `card_ids` of the submitted order. Do not call this endpoint when the order amount is 0, for sell orders, when the Client has already selected a cash card manually, for trailing stop limit orders, or for multi-leg orders. When no card is available, `card_id` is empty. To get the full list of available and unavailable cards, use `GET /v1/commssion/rebate/list`.

post.description:
Submits a non-option order for stocks, ETFs, warrants, and similar securities. It covers limit, market, enhanced limit, auction, odd-lot, order-by-amount (US fractional shares), conditional orders (`SLO`, `LIT`, `MIT`), trailing stop, market on close, attached orders (take-profit, stop-loss, bracket), and pre-market, after-hours, and overnight sessions. Before submission, the Client should have confirmed the order on the order page and unlocked trading. The order type, session, time in force, and attached order must be within the ranges returned by Get Order Configuration, and the required authorizations and declarations must be completed. This endpoint is also used by the day-trade margin order panel and by order cards in AI conversations.

A successful response means the order has been accepted, not filled. Use the order details or order push to track its status. After success, if `notice` is not empty, show the trading reminder to the Client, then refresh the order list and assets. On failure, show `message` to the Client so the Client can modify the order and resubmit.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `submitOrder`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Stock Order” operation.

Submits a single-leg option order. The request parameters are the same as Submit Stock Order: pass the option contract ID in `counter_id` and the number of contracts in `quantity`; you can also pass `stock_contract` to describe the contract. Before submission, the Client should have confirmed the order and unlocked trading. This endpoint is also used by option order cards in AI conversations. For multi-leg combinations, use Submit Multi-Leg Option Order.

A successful response means the order has been accepted, not filled. Use the order details or order push to track its status. After success, if `notice` is not empty, show the trading reminder to the Client, then refresh the order list and assets. On failure, show `message` to the Client so the Client can modify the order and resubmit.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` provides the corresponding capability. If you use WhaleCore, prefer the corresponding `orderService()` method.

post.description:
Submits a multi-leg option combination order, such as covered, vertical spread, collar, straddle, strangle, and calendar spread. In addition to the parameters of Submit Stock Order, pass `strategy` and `legs`: `counter_id` is the main security (the underlying stock), `quantity` is the combination quantity, `price` is the combination limit price, and each leg's `ratio_quantity` comes from Get Multi-Leg Option Order Configuration. Multi-leg orders do not support attached orders. Before submission, the Client should have confirmed the order and unlocked trading. This endpoint is also used by multi-leg option order cards in AI conversations.

A successful response means the order has been accepted, not filled. Use the order details or order push to track its status. After success, if `notice` is not empty, show the trading reminder to the Client, then refresh the order list and assets. On failure, show `message` to the Client so the Client can modify the order and resubmit.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` provides the corresponding capability. If you use WhaleCore, prefer the corresponding `orderService()` method.

- `4` - Collar

post.summary: Submit Position Take-Profit and Stop-Loss Orders
post.description:
Places take-profit and/or stop-loss conditional orders for an existing position at once, used by the position's take-profit and stop-loss panel. Unlike attached orders, position take-profit and stop-loss orders act on the existing position and do not depend on a new main order. Derive the side from the position: pass `2` (sell) for a long position and `1` (buy) for a short position. Set at least one of take-profit and stop-loss; both use the same order type. On success, the response returns the group ID `ploy_id`, which links the take-profit and stop-loss orders placed in this request in the order list. The placed orders are regular conditional orders, so amend and cancel them as conditional orders. On failure, show `message` to the Client.

WhaleCore's `orderService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `submitTPSLOrder`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

settlement_currency.description: Settlement currency, such as USD or HKD. Use an item of `channel_infos.settlement_currency` returned by Get Order Configuration

action.description:
Closing side:
- `1` - Buy (short position)
- `2` - Sell (long position)

quantity.description: Order quantity of the take-profit and stop-loss orders

time_in_force.description:
Time in force. The value must be in `support_time_in_forces` of the order type in Get Order Configuration:
- `0` - Day (DAY)
- `1` - Good till canceled (GTC)
- `3` - Immediate or cancel (IOC)
- `5` - Fill or kill (FOK)
- `6` - Good till date (GTD); `expire_time` is also required

If omitted, the order is treated as a day order.

expire_time.description: Expiry time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Required when `time_in_force` is `6`

force_only_rth.description:
Trading session (pass it when the security supports pre-market and after-hours trading):
- `1` - Regular trading hours only
- `2` - Regular trading hours plus pre-market and after-hours

take_profit_order_type.description:
Take-profit order type:
- `LIT` - Limit if touched; the matching `*_submit_price` is also required
- `MIT` - Market if touched

take_profit_trigger_price.description: Take-profit trigger price. Required when take-profit is set

take_profit_submit_price.description: Limit price after the take-profit order triggers. Required when `take_profit_order_type` is `LIT`

stop_loss_order_type.description:
Stop-loss order type:
- `LIT` - Limit if touched; the matching `*_submit_price` is also required
- `MIT` - Market if touched

stop_loss_trigger_price.description: Stop-loss trigger price. Required when stop-loss is set

stop_loss_submit_price.description: Limit price after the stop-loss order triggers. Required when `stop_loss_order_type` is `LIT`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Position Take-Profit and Stop-Loss Orders” operation.

post.description:
After the Client selects the grid trading order type on the order page and sets the rules, creates a grid trading strategy: around the base price, the strategy sells according to the rules each time the price rises to the trigger condition and buys each time it falls to the trigger condition, for as long as the strategy is valid. When the price leaves the range, it is handled according to `upper_limit_event` / `lower_limit_event`. Grid trading applies only to stock-type securities, does not support options or China A-shares, and requires the Broker to enable the capability for the tenant. Before submission, the Client should have agreed to the grid trading risk declaration (`channel_infos.strategy_granted` is `true` in Get Order Configuration) and unlocked trading. On success, the response returns the grid order ID, which you can use to track the strategy. On failure, show `message` to the Client.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

settlement_currency.description: Settlement currency, such as USD or HKD. Use an item of `channel_infos.settlement_currency` returned by Get Order Configuration

client_request_id.description: Client request identifier: the millisecond timestamp at submission

get.description:
Retrieves the crypto tokens that the current account can deposit or withdraw, together with their configuration: available networks, whether deposits and withdrawals are supported, per-transaction minimums, quantity precision, whether a deposit requires an extra verification amount, and whether professional investor (PI) verification is required.

Show only tokens with `support_deposit` set to `yes` on the deposit page, and only tokens with `support_withdraw` set to `yes` on the withdrawal page. When `pi_verify` is `yes`, the Client must complete professional investor verification before depositing or withdrawing.

This endpoint is also used on the whitelisted address management page to build the network filter from the deduplicated `chain_types` of all tokens.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Crypto Token List” operation.

chain_types.description: Available networks, separated by commas, such as `ETH,TRON`. When there is only one network, you can preselect it.

support_deposit.description: Whether deposits are supported: `yes` means supported; any other value means not supported.

support_withdraw.description: Whether withdrawals are supported: `yes` means supported; any other value means not supported.

pi_verify.description: Whether depositing or withdrawing this token requires professional investor verification: `yes` means required.

deposit_need_micro_verification.description: Whether every deposit must include a randomly generated verification amount: `yes` means required even from a whitelisted address; `no` means not required.

min_per_deposit.description: Minimum quantity per deposit in the token, as a decimal string.

min_per_withdraw.description: Minimum quantity per withdrawal in the token, as a decimal string. If the estimated fee is higher, the fee becomes the minimum withdrawal quantity.

quantity_precision.description: Number of decimal places for quantities. Limit the input accordingly; when it is `0` or missing, the client uses 8.

conversion_currency.description: Fiat currency used for valuation on withdrawal. Pass it as `exchange_currency` when submitting a withdrawal request.

get.description:
Retrieves, when the withdrawal page loads, the holding quantity and withdrawable quantity of each token in the current account, together with the daily withdrawal count limit. Use it to show the available amount, validate the maximum withdrawal quantity, and show the remaining withdrawals today.

The withdrawal quantity must not exceed `available_quantity`. When `remaining_times` is `0`, the daily withdrawal count is used up; block submission and ask the Client to try again the next day. Call this endpoint again after a withdrawal request is submitted.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Query only this token. Omit it to return all tokens.

parameters.name: need_fiat_balance
parameters.description: Whether to also return the fiat cash balance of the securities account. The withdrawal page passes `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Crypto Withdrawal Preview” operation.

items.description: Holding and withdrawable quantity by token.

total_quantity.description: Holding quantity of the token, as a decimal string.

available_quantity.description: Quantity of the token that can be withdrawn now, as a decimal string. The withdrawal quantity must not exceed it.

limits.description: Withdrawal count limits. The client uses the first item.

frequency_limit.description: Total number of withdrawals allowed per day.

remaining_times.description: Number of withdrawals left today. When it is `0`, no further withdrawal request can be submitted.

post.description:
Retrieves the current USD price `last_done` of the specified tokens. The withdrawal page calls it after the Client enters a quantity, then passes the price as `usd_rate` to Estimate Crypto Withdrawal Fee and as `exchange_rate` when submitting the withdrawal request.

If `last_done` is missing or `0`, do not estimate the fee or submit the withdrawal request. This endpoint is read-only and has no side effects.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Crypto Prices” operation.

items.description: Prices in the same order as the requested `coins`.

last_done.description: Latest price, as a decimal string.

get.description:
Estimates the withdrawal fee for a token, network, and quantity. The fee has two parts: the crypto fee (`crypto_fee`) deducted from the withdrawn crypto, and the account service fee (`fiat_fee`) deducted from the available cash in the securities account.

Call it after the Client stops typing (the page uses a debounce of about 500 ms). The estimated amount to receive is the withdrawal quantity minus the crypto fee; when `crypto_fee` is empty, use `fee`. If the available cash in the securities account cannot cover the account service fee, the withdrawal request cannot be submitted. If the request fails, clear the fee display and block submission.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Token symbol, such as `BTC`, `ETH`, or `USDT`, taken from `coin` in Get Crypto Token List.

parameters.name: chain_type
parameters.description: Network (chain) name, one of the values in the token `chain_types`.

parameters.description: Quantity to withdraw, as a decimal string.

parameters.name: usd_rate

parameters.description: Whether to return the crypto fee and its breakdown. The withdrawal page passes `true`.

parameters.name: need_fiat_fee
parameters.description: Whether to return the account service fee and its breakdown. The withdrawal page passes `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Estimate Crypto Withdrawal Fee” operation.

fee.description: Withdrawal fee in the token. Kept for compatibility; when `crypto_fee` has a value, use `crypto_fee`.

crypto_fee.description: Crypto fee in the token, deducted from the withdrawal quantity.

fiat_currency.description: Currency of the account service fee.

fiat_fee.description: Account service fee, deducted from the available cash in the securities account. Do not show it when it is empty or not greater than 0.

fiat_fee_details.description: Breakdown of the account service fee.

get.description:
Checks, after the Client selects an existing whitelisted address on the deposit or withdrawal page, whether the address can currently be used to deposit or withdraw the selected token.

A successful response means the address is usable. A business error means it is not; mark the address as unavailable, block submission, and ask the Client to contact customer support. Do not call this endpoint when the Client chooses to add a new address.

parameters.name: wallet_id
parameters.description: Whitelisted address id, taken from `wallet_id` in Query Whitelisted Address List.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Token symbol, such as `BTC`, `ETH`, or `USDT`, taken from `coin` in Get Crypto Token List.

parameters.name: business_type
parameters.description:
Business type:
- `Deposit` - Crypto deposit
- `Withdraw` - Crypto withdrawal

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Whitelisted Address Availability” operation.

data.description: No business fields. A successful response means the check passed.

get.description:
Checks the crypto holding concentration of the current account after the Client selects a token on the deposit page and before the deposit form opens, and returns the risk reasons to show to the Client.

If `reasons` is empty, open the deposit form directly. Otherwise, show the first reason to the Client and ask for confirmation; the Client can still continue after confirming. If the token `pi_verify` is `yes`, confirm that the Client has completed professional investor verification before calling this endpoint. If the request fails, show `message` and stay on the current page.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Concentration Before Crypto Deposit” operation.

reasons.description: Concentration risk reasons to show to the Client as is. Empty means no prompt is needed.

post.description:
Submits a crypto deposit request for a token, network, and deposit method, and returns the receiving address of this account and the final quantity the Client must transfer. The Client must transfer exactly `required_deposit_quantity` from their own wallet to `deposit_address`; otherwise the deposit may fail.

The deposit method is set by `business_type`. When depositing from a new address (`auth`) or when the token requires a verification amount (`trade_auth`), the system generates a random verification amount, and the final quantity is the intended quantity plus the verification amount; show the receiving address after the Client confirms. After a deposit from a new address succeeds, the address is added to the Client whitelist automatically.

Side effects: creates a deposit request that appears in Query Crypto Deposit Records. While its status is `pending_auth`, it can be cancelled with `POST /v1/atm/va/coin/deposit/cancel`. If the Client changes the quantity and submits again, a new verification amount is generated. On failure, show `message` instead of resubmitting immediately.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

A complete deposit flow runs in this order: get the token list (`GET /v1/atm/va/query/all/coin/list`) → confirm professional investor verification when required → check concentration (`GET /v1/atm/va/coin/concentration/check`) → select a network and query whitelisted addresses (`POST /v1/atm/va/query/client/wallet/address/list`) → check availability when an existing address is selected (`GET /v1/atm/va/validate/client/wallet/available`) → submit the deposit request → the Client transfers the returned quantity to the returned address → query deposit records.

coin.description: Token symbol, such as `BTC`, `ETH`, or `USDT`, taken from `coin` in Get Crypto Token List.

chain_type.description: Network (chain) name, one of the values in the token `chain_types`.

business_type.description:
Deposit method:
- `normal` - Deposit from a verified whitelisted address
- `trade_auth` - Deposit from a whitelisted address for a token that requires a verification amount (`deposit_need_micro_verification` is `yes`)
- `auth` - Deposit from a new address, with a verification amount to verify the address

quantity.description: Intended deposit quantity as a decimal string, not below the token `min_per_deposit`. Pass `"0"` when no quantity is entered.

wallet_id.description: Whitelisted address id. Pass `0` or omit it when `business_type` is `auth` (new address).

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Crypto Deposit Request” operation.

deposit_address.description: Receiving address of this account on the network. The Client must transfer to this address.

required_deposit_quantity.description: Final quantity the Client must transfer (intended quantity plus any verification amount). It must match exactly.

random_verify_quantity.description: Randomly generated verification amount. It can be empty when no verification is needed.

post.description:
Cancels a crypto deposit request whose address verification is not yet complete. Only records with the status `pending_auth` (verifying) can be cancelled, and cancellation cannot be undone.

Side effects: the deposit record enters cancellation (`canceling`, then `cancelled` or `cancel_failed`). Ask the Client to confirm first. On success, query the record again to refresh its status; on failure, show `message`.

id.description: Deposit record id, taken from `id` in Query Crypto Deposit Records.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Cancel Crypto Deposit Request” operation.

post.description:
Submits a crypto withdrawal request with the token, network, quantity, and whitelisted receiving address, and returns the withdrawal record id once accepted. Acceptance means only that the request was submitted; the outcome is determined by the withdrawal record status.

Preconditions: the receiving address is active in the whitelist (addresses marked by `is_pending_effect` cannot be selected) and has passed the availability check; the quantity does not exceed `available_quantity` from Get Crypto Withdrawal Preview and is not below the larger of `min_per_withdraw` and the estimated crypto fee; the remaining withdrawals today are greater than `0`; the token price and fee estimate have been retrieved; and the available cash in the securities account can cover the account service fee.

Side effects: creates a withdrawal request and reserves the withdrawable quantity. On success, use the returned `id` with Query Crypto Withdrawal Records to show the details, and refresh the withdrawal preview. On failure, show `message` instead of resubmitting immediately.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

A complete withdrawal flow runs in this order: get the token list and the withdrawal preview (`GET /v1/atm/va/query/all/coin/list`, `GET /v1/atm/va/withdraw/coin/preview`) → select a network and a whitelisted address and check its availability → get the token price (`POST /v1/atm/va/get/coin/prices`) → estimate the fee (`GET /v1/atm/va/estimate/coin/fee`) → submit the withdrawal request → query withdrawal records.

coin.description: Token symbol, such as `BTC`, `ETH`, or `USDT`, taken from `coin` in Get Crypto Token List.

chain_type.description: Network (chain) name, one of the values in the token `chain_types`.

quantity.description: Withdrawal quantity, as a decimal string.

wallet_id.description: Whitelisted receiving address id, taken from `wallet_id` in Query Whitelisted Address List.

exchange_currency.description: Valuation currency, taken from the token `conversion_currency`.

exchange_rate.description: Token price, taken from `last_done` in Get Crypto Prices.

need_crypto_fee.description: Whether to apply the crypto fee. Keep it consistent with the fee estimate; the withdrawal page passes `true`.

need_fiat_fee.description: Whether to apply the account service fee. Keep it consistent with the fee estimate; the withdrawal page passes `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Crypto Withdrawal Request” operation.

id.description: Withdrawal record id, usable as `id` in Query Crypto Withdrawal Records.

post.description:
Retrieves the crypto deposit records of the current account by page, with optional filters for time, token, and status. When `id` is provided, only that record is returned, for the deposit details page.

If fewer records than `page_size` are returned, there are no more pages. Records with the status `pending_auth` can be cancelled with `POST /v1/atm/va/coin/deposit/cancel`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Query Crypto Deposit Records” operation.

quantity.description: Deposit quantity.

status_text.description: Display text of the status, to show as is.

wallet_name.description: Whitelist name of the sending address.

is_white_verify.description: Whether this is an address-verification deposit: `yes` means it is, and you can label it as address verification.

remark.description: Additional note, such as the failure reason. Show it when present.

created_at.description: Creation time. Unix timestamp as a string. It can be 10 digits (seconds) or 13 digits (milliseconds); detect the unit by length when parsing.

updated_at.description: Last update time. Unix timestamp as a string. It can be 10 digits (seconds) or 13 digits (milliseconds); detect the unit by length when parsing.

post.description:
Retrieves the crypto withdrawal records of the current account by page, with optional filters for time, token, and status. When `id` is provided, only that record is returned, for the withdrawal details and result pages.

If fewer records than `page_size` are returned, there are no more pages. While the status is `processing`, the received quantity is not final; show `required_quantity` minus the crypto fee as the estimate. When the status is `failed`, do not show the fee.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Query Crypto Withdrawal Records” operation.

net_quantity.description: Quantity received after the crypto fee. Not final while the status is `processing`.

fee_quantity.description: Withdrawal fee in the token. Kept for compatibility; when `crypto_fee` has a value, use `crypto_fee`.

A newly whitelisted address becomes active after about 30 minutes; an address marked by `is_pending_effect` cannot be used for withdrawals. After the upload succeeds, submit `key` to the business endpoint that needs the attachment.

This endpoint is used for file uploads in several features, including stock transfer-in attachments, account opening documents, professional investor verification materials, and electronic signatures. If an upload fails, get a new upload URL and upload again.

get.description:
Returns the amount available for currency exchange in each currency of the current account. The currency exchange page shows it as the “cash available” or “maximum available” amount for each source currency in the currency picker, and uses it as the upper limit of the source amount. `list` may contain multiple currencies; the Broker App selects the entry by `currency`.

Each currency has two figures: `available_amount` covers cash only; `available_amount_with_mmf` also includes the money market fund (MMF) portion that can be redeemed automatically. Use the latter only when the Broker enables automatic MMF redemption for currency exchange (submissions then use `POST /v1/forex/reserve/convert`); fall back to `available_amount` when it is missing. The difference between the two is the amount that MMF redemption can cover.

post.summary: Batch Estimate Exchange Amounts and Funding Sources
post.description:
Estimates, in batch, the amount on one side from the source/target currencies and the amount on the other side, and returns the reference exchange rate (including markup). Used to estimate the other amount in real time while the Client enters the source or target amount on the currency exchange page, and to show the amounts in the confirmation dialog before submission.

The request body is the same as `POST /v1/atm/calc/multi/estimate/exchange/amount`. The difference is that each estimate in the response is wrapped in `item` and includes `cash_used` and `mmf_redeem`. When automatic MMF redemption for currency exchange is enabled, the Broker App uses them to show the cash amount used and the MMF amount to be redeemed in the confirmation dialog (`mmf_redeem` greater than `0` means the exchange redeems the MMF).

Estimates are for display only; the final amounts are those in the exchange record. If the request fails, show the rate as unavailable and do not submit with a previous estimate.

get.description:
Returns the activation status of the money market fund (MMF) automatic subscription for the current account. When automatic MMF redemption for currency exchange is enabled, the currency exchange page calls it and shows the MMF exchangeable amount only when `mmf_status` is `1`.

It is also used for MMF subscription management. Before opening the subscription management page and before saving automatic subscription settings, `mmf_status` and `mmf_version` determine whether the action is activation, upgrade, or update (`mmf_status` other than `1`: activation; `mmf_status` `1` and `mmf_version` other than `1`: upgrade; `mmf_version` `1`: update). The asset analysis page also queries it on load.

parameters.description: Broker channel

- `0` - Not activated
- `1` - Activated
- `2` - Activating
- `3` - Deactivating

Whether the new MMF version that supports multiple money market funds is activated:

- `0` - Not activated
- `1` - Activated

post.description:
Submits a currency exchange request whose funding can be topped up by automatic MMF redemption. When the Broker enables automatic MMF redemption for currency exchange, the Broker App submits exchanges through this endpoint instead of `POST /v1/forex/convert`; any part of the source amount beyond the exchangeable cash is covered by redeeming the MMF. Submit by either the source amount (`amount`) or the target amount (`target_amount`), not both.

Before submission, show the amounts and the cash/MMF split from `POST /v1/forex/calc/multi/estimate/exchange/amount` in a confirmation dialog, and submit after the Client confirms. `id` and `reserve_no` are mutually exclusive, and the one that does not apply is `0`. When querying details with `GET /v1/forex/convert/detail` or cancelling with `POST /v1/forex/front/cancel/exchange`, pass `reserve_no` for a reserved order whose `reserve_no` is not `0`. When `in_service` is `false`, tell the Client the estimated completion time from `deal_time`. On failure, show `message` to the Client.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

amount.description: Source amount, when submitting by source amount; provide either this or `target_amount`

target_amount.description: Target amount, when submitting by target amount; provide either this or `amount`

cancel_on_rate_change.description:
Exchange rate protection:

- `0` - Do not act on rate changes
- `1` - Cancel this exchange automatically if the rate moves by more than 0.3%

The Broker App passes `1` only when the exchange redeems the MMF (`mmf_redeem` in the estimate is greater than `0`) and the Client selects the option; otherwise it passes `0`.

post.description:
Submits a request to transfer stocks from another broker into the current account. Typical flow: select the market (`GET /v2/portfolio/rollover/markets`) → select the delivering broker (`GET /v1/portfolio/rollover/brokers`) → search for and fill in the stocks (`GET /v1/portfolio/stocks/search`) → optionally upload supporting documents → confirm and call this endpoint.

A successful call means only that the request has been accepted; the stocks arrive after the delivering broker processes the transfer. On success, show the receiving broker information (`GET /v3/portfolio/rollover/receiver`) and guide the Client to notify the delivering broker; after the Client confirms, call `POST /portfolio/rollover/mark`. Then track progress with `GET /v3/portfolio/rollover/record` and `GET /v2/portfolio/rollover/detail/{id}`. On failure, show `message` to the Client and resubmit after correction.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

post.description: Returns the indicator settings the current user saved, by indicator ID. Use it when the chart loads to restore the user's custom indicator parameters, line colors, and indicator selection and order. An ID can be an indicator ID returned by `GET /v2/indicator/get_all_indicator`, or a chart-position configuration key used to save the indicator selection and order. post.description: Saves the current user's settings for one indicator or one chart position, overwriting what was previously saved for that ID. There are two uses: after the user changes parameters and lines on the indicator settings page, save the parameter and line configuration under the indicator ID; after the user selects or reorders indicators in the indicator panel, save the list of selected indicator IDs under the chart-position configuration key. After a successful save, other devices read the new settings through `POST /v1/indicator/get_config`. The Broker App updates its local settings before calling this endpoint; if the call fails, tell the user and keep the local settings so the save can be retried.

When saving under an indicator ID, the structure is `{"params": {<parameter key>: {"value": <number>}}, "charts": {<line key>: {"is_selected": <boolean>, "color": <hex color>}}}`. When saving under a chart-position configuration key, the structure is `{"configs": [<indicator ID>, ...]}`, and the array order is the display order.

200.description: The request succeeded. A `code` of `0` means the settings were saved.

The US index chart on the market page also uses this operation to load intraday prices for several indexes at once with the intraday period.

get.description: Returns the interest disclosure text for an ETF, shown with the prefix “Interest disclosure:” in the disclaimer area at the bottom of the ETF detail page. Call it only for ETFs. When `content` is empty or the request fails, do not show the disclosure.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID in the format `ST/<market>/<code>`, such as `ST/HK/2800`

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Disclosure type. Always send `profit_sharing`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get ETF Interest Disclosure” operation.

content.description: Disclosure text. Empty when nothing should be shown

post.description:
Returns paged news content for a channel. The News list under News on the security detail page uses the `stock_news` channel and sends the current security in `counter_ids`. IPO News in the IPO center uses the `ipo_news` channel and sends only `limit` and the previous page's `next_params`.

To load the next page, send back `next_params` from the previous response unchanged. When `articles` is empty, there is no more content.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description:
Channel ID:

- `stock_news` - Security news
- `ipo_news` - IPO news

limit.description: Items per page. The Broker App sends 20

counter_ids.description: Filter by security, such as `ST/HK/700`. Required for the `stock_news` channel

next_params.description: Pagination parameters. Send an empty object for the first page, then the previous response's `next_params` unchanged

has_derivatives.description: Whether to return related securities and their quotes

important_only.description: Whether to return only important news

market.description: Filter by market. Send an empty string for security news

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List Channel News” operation.

next_params.description: Pagination parameters for the next page

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID in the format `ST/<market>/<code>`, such as `ST/HK/700`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Security News Badges” operation.

get.description: Returns hot news for a concept or industry sector, for the Hot news block on the sector detail page. The Broker App shows the first 3 items.

parameters.name: concept_index
parameters.description: Security ID of the sector, which is the `counter_id` of the sector detail page

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Sector Hot News” operation.

publish_at.description: Publication time as a Unix timestamp, in seconds

get.description:
Returns an ETF profile: fund name and introduction, asset class, fund size, investment geography, benchmark index, risk level, fund company, Morningstar rating, and investment style box. Use it for the Overview section on the ETF detail page.

The same operation also serves the rating display on the security detail page and the investment style section (style box with style and size text). Show the investment style section only when `invest_style_grid` is greater than 0 and both the style and size text are not empty.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the ETF, such as `ETF/US/SPY`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get ETF Profile” operation.

data.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
data.profile: The fund seeks to track the performance of the S&P 500 Index.

post.description: Returns ETF fund information: name, type, tracked index, leverage, total expense ratio and management fee, introduction, dividend policy, net asset value, shares outstanding, listing date, fund manager, and custodian. Use it for the fund information block in the Overview section on the ETF detail page. The operation only reads data and has no side effects. When the request fails, Broker App shows an empty state.

counter_id.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the ETF, such as `ETF/US/SPY`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get ETF Fund Information” operation.

data.description: The fund seeks to track the performance of the S&P 500 Index.
data.custodian: State Street Bank and Trust Company

get.description: Returns quote details for an index or sector index: last price, previous close, quote time, net capital inflow, and the number of rising, falling, and unchanged constituents. Use it for the change, capital inflow, and advance-decline display in the header of the concept sector detail page. Compute the change percentage from `last_done` and `prev_close`.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the index or sector index, such as the concept sector index `BK/HK/LB20000`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Index Quote Details” operation.

timestamp.description: Quote time

inflow.description: Net capital inflow. A positive value is a net inflow and a negative value is a net outflow

get.description: Returns the constituents of an index with quote summaries (last price, change, net capital inflow, turnover, turnover rate, market capitalization, and more), paginated and sorted by an indicator. Use it for the Constituents list on the index detail page. Paginate with `offset` and `limit`: pass `0` as `offset` for the first page and add `limit` for each further page. Stop loading when the number of loaded items reaches `total`.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the index, such as `IX/HK/HSTECH`

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Offset, starting from 0

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of items per page. Broker App passes 200

parameters.name: indicator
parameters.description:
Sort indicator:

- `1` - Change percentage (default)
- `2` - Last price
- `3` - Turnover
- `4` - Capital flow
- `5` - Turnover rate
- `6` - Market capitalization

For indexes without quotes, Broker App always passes `12`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description:
Sort direction:

- `0` - Descending (default)
- `1` - Ascending

parameters.name: sort_type
parameters.description:
Legacy sort mode, superseded by `indicator` and `order`. Broker App always passes `0`:

- `0` - Change, high to low
- `1` - Change, low to high
- `2` - Last price, high to low
- `3` - Last price, low to high

parameters.name: bmp
parameters.description: Whether the current user receives Hong Kong BMP (snapshot) quotes

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Index Constituents” operation.

get.description: Returns the name of an industry sector and the corresponding sector security in each market. Use it for the market switcher in the title of the industry sector detail page: after a market is selected, reopen the detail page with that market's `counter_id`. Broker App drops markets whose `counter_id` is empty and shows only markets that the current Broker supports (`SH` and `SZ` count as `CN`).

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the industry sector, such as `BK/US/IN00276`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Industry Sector Markets” operation.

markets.description: Sector securities of the industry in each market

get.description: Returns introduction information for a concept sector: name, introduction, sector index and benchmark index, and banner and cover images. Use it for the concept introduction block in the Overview section on the concept sector detail page. Broker App hides the block when `intro` is empty or when the request fails.

parameters.name: concept_index
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the concept sector index, such as `BK/HK/LB20000`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Concept Sector Introduction” operation.

data.title: Artificial intelligence
