get.description:
Returns several groups of combined search results for a keyword in one call. Use it for the All tab on the search results page: security candidates (`product_list`), recommended search terms (`recommend_list`), and related news (`news_list`). Security results use the same fields as Search securities. Do not call it with an empty keyword. When the input changes, use the response for the latest keyword and discard stale responses.

The response can also contain groups such as community and help center results. These groups are platform-owned content, are not documented here, and Brokers should ignore them.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Search keyword. Enter a security code, name, or news keyword

parameters.name: search_src
parameters.description: Source scenario of the search. Pass `main_search` for combined search

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel of the current account. Pass an empty string when the user has no account

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Search All Content” operation.

product_list.description: Matching security candidates. It is an empty array when nothing matches

isin.description: International Securities Identification Number (ISIN). Fund results often show it instead of the code. It can be empty for other products

news_list.title: Apple unveils new iPhone
news_list.description: Apple introduced its new iPhone lineup at its fall event.
news_list.description_en: Apple introduced its new iPhone lineup at its fall event.

get.summary: Get Listed Code for Unlisted Security
get.description: Returns the new security ID that an unlisted security (such as a pre-IPO company) received after listing. Call it before opening a detail link that points to an unlisted security: if `new_counter_id` is not empty, open the detail page of the new security; if it is empty or the request fails, open the original security ID. Security links in rich text such as news and posts use this operation.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (`counter_id`) of the unlisted security

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Listed Code for Unlisted Security” operation.

new_counter_id.description: New security ID after listing. It is empty when the security is not listed yet or has no mapping

get.summary: Get analyst rating distribution and target price trend
get.description:
Return, as time series, the analyst rating distribution of the specified stock (number of institutions rating Strong buy, Buy, Hold, Underperform, Sell, or no opinion) and the target price trend (highest and lowest target prices forecast by institutions and the stock price at the same time). Used by the analyst rating block in the stock detail Overview and by the rating distribution and target price charts on the rating detail page.

When elist is empty, the Broker App hides the analyst rating block. When calculating rating shares, the Broker App uses the sum of the first five rating counts as the denominator and excludes no opinion.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get analyst rating distribution and target price trend” operation.

elist.description: Rating distribution time series in ascending time order

tlist.description: Target price time series in ascending time order

get.summary: Get the industries of a stock
get.description: Return the primary industry of the specified stock and the industry sectors it belongs to at each level (primary, secondary, micro) with their counter_id. Used by the Industry data block of the stock Overview (shown by the Broker App in the Overview of new listings during grey market trading). The Broker App then queries quotes by each sector counter_id to show sector price changes.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get the industries of a stock” operation.

industries.description: Industry sectors the stock belongs to

get.summary: Get a stock's indicator rankings within its industry
get.description:
Return, for the specified stock, the value, ranking, industry average, median, and interval distribution of each indicator within its industry (such as market value, operating revenue, and net profit), plus the number of companies in the industry and the amount currency. Used by the industry ranking in the Industry data block of the stock Overview.

Also used by the industry ranking on the web stock encyclopedia page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Industry ID; not passed by the Broker App

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market, such as `US`; not passed by the Broker App

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get a stock's indicator rankings within its industry” operation.

get.description:
Return the ranking details of each indicator within the industry (value and ranking of the current underlying, industry average, median, and interval distribution), with the same structure as "Get a stock's indicator rankings within its industry". Pass counter_id to query by stock and get its ranking within its industry; pass fcounter_id to query by industry on the industry sector detail page.

Used by the industry ranking comparison on the stock Financials page and by the industry ranking detail page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`. Pass it to query by stock; use either this or fcounter_id

parameters.name: fcounter_id
parameters.description: Industry sector counter_id, such as `BK/US/IN00276`. Pass it to query by industry; use either this or counter_id

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency for amount statistics. The Broker App passes the currency of the market where the underlying is listed, such as `USD` or `HKD`

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Industry ID; not passed by the Broker App

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market, such as `US`; not passed by the Broker App

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get industry indicator ranking details” operation.

get.summary: Get the industry ranking list of one indicator
get.description:
Return, for one indicator code, the value and ranking of each company in the industry, mark the current underlying, and return the industry summary of the indicator (average, median, interval distribution). Pass counter_id to query by stock, or fcounter_id to query by industry.

Used when switching indicators on the industry ranking detail page, by the industry ranking curve in the stock Overview, and by the Industry data block on the industry sector detail page when switching between market value, total assets, operating revenue, and net profit.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`. Pass it to query by stock; use either this or fcounter_id

parameters.name: fcounter_id
parameters.description: Industry sector counter_id, such as `BK/US/IN00276`. Pass it to query by industry; use either this or counter_id

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency for amount statistics. The Broker App passes the currency of the market where the underlying is listed, such as `USD` or `HKD`

parameters.name: code
parameters.description:
Indicator code. Known values:

- `market_value` - Market value
- `total_assets` - Total assets
- `operating_revenue` - Operating revenue
- `net_profit` - Net profit

parameters.name: industry
parameters.description: Industry ID; not passed by the Broker App

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market, such as `US`; not passed by the Broker App

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Page size; the Broker App passes `20`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get the industry ranking list of one indicator” operation.

total.description: Total number of companies in the industry

get.summary: Get financial distribution of industry constituents
get.description: Return the total market value, total assets, operating revenue, and net profit of all constituents of an industry sector, plus each constituent's values and shares, PE, ROE, and year-over-year operating revenue growth. Used by the pie chart and constituent list in the Industry data block on the industry sector detail page. order_by sets the indicator used to sort the constituent list.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Industry sector counter_id, such as `BK/US/IN00276`

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency for amount statistics. The Broker App passes the currency of the market where the underlying is listed, such as `USD` or `HKD`

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description:
Indicator for sorting constituents:

- `market_value` - Market value
- `total_assets` - Total assets
- `operating_revenue` - Operating revenue
- `net_profit` - Net profit

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get financial distribution of industry constituents” operation.

get.summary: Get financial history of an industry sector
get.description: Return, by year, the total market value, total assets, operating revenue, and net profit of the constituents of an industry sector and the number of companies. Used by the history bar chart in the Industry data block on the industry sector detail page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Industry sector counter_id, such as `BK/US/IN00276`

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency for amount statistics. The Broker App passes the currency of the market where the underlying is listed, such as `USD` or `HKD`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get financial history of an industry sector” operation.

count.description: Number of constituents in the period

get.summary: Get stocks with a similar investment style
get.description:
Return recommended stocks with an investment style similar to the specified stock (name, introduction, logo, market, total market value, number of followers). Used by the Similar-style stocks in the investment style block of the stock Overview and its full list page. The Broker App then queries quotes by counter_id to show price changes.

Uses cursor paging: pass `0` as last_id for the first page and the id of the last item of the previous page for the next page. An empty list means there is no more data.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: last_id
parameters.description: Paging cursor: id of the last item of the previous page; pass `0` for the first page

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of items; the Broker App passes `4` for the block and `10` for the list page

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get stocks with a similar investment style” operation.

items.name: Microsoft
items.description: Global software and cloud services provider

get.description:
Return, in one call, the aggregated summary at the top of the stock Overview: ranking tags, the industry sector and its top-level node in the industry tree, related concept sectors, and investment style (style index, size score, style score, grid position). Used by the summary at the top of the stock detail Overview. The Broker App then queries quotes by the industry and concept sector counter_id.

Community watchlist content in the response is not covered by this document.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of related items; the Broker App passes `3`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get stock overview summary” operation.

change.description: Style index price change as a decimal, such as `0.0123` for 1.23%

invest_style_grid.description: Position number in the investment style grid

top.description: Top-level node of the industry in the industry tree

total.description: Total number of related concept sectors

get.description:
Return the panorama at the top of the stock Overview: company introduction and logo (unlisted_logo for unlisted underlyings), ranking tags, the industry sector with its quote snapshot, and related concept sectors. Used by the company introduction, ranking tags, and industry and concept blocks at the top of the stock detail Overview. The Broker App then queries quotes by concept sector counter_id.

This operation already includes the primary industry and related concepts, so separate industry or concept queries are not needed.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get stock panorama” operation.

intro.description: One-line introduction; when empty, the Broker App shows profile

icon.description: Icon URL; logo is used when empty

logo.description: Company information of a listed underlying

unlisted_logo.description: Company information of an unlisted underlying

tags.description: Label groups; the Broker App only shows labels whose target_type is `TopRankTag`

target_type.description: Label type; `TopRankTag` is a ranking tag

target_id.description: ID of the object the label points to, such as a ranking list key

securities.description: Quote snapshot of the industry sector; the Broker App uses the first item to show the industry price change

logo.name: Apple
logo.intro: Global consumer electronics and software services company
logo.profile: The company designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories, and sells related services.

get.summary: Get module switches of the stock analysis page
get.description:
Return whether each module of the stock Analysis page is available for the current client and underlying, plus the deep data page URL. Used when opening the Analysis page to decide which tabs to show: financial score, business commentary, investment style, analyst rating, and valuation analysis.

Broker App rule: for clients with an opened account, industry_ratings_enable decides whether the financial score is shown; for clients without an opened account, is_done_risk, agreement_enable, and industry_ratings_enable must all be true. When the request fails, the Broker App leaves the Analysis page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get module switches of the stock analysis page” operation.

industry_ratings_enable.description: Whether the financial score is available

agreement_enable.description: Whether the client has signed the score data risk agreement

is_done_risk.description: Whether the client has completed the risk assessment

custom_module_url.description: Deep data page URL; empty when there is none

get.description: Return the text introduction of an industry sector, used by the industry introduction at the top of the Overview on the industry sector detail page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Industry sector counter_id, such as `BK/US/IN00276`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get industry sector introduction” operation.

data.intro: The consumer electronics industry covers the design and manufacturing of devices such as smartphones, personal computers, and wearables.

get.description: Returns whether the security has in-depth data, plus the title and description of the chart shown on the entry card, for the in-depth data card on the stock overview and Analysis tabs. When `exist` is `false`, the Broker App hides the entry. Fetch the in-depth data itself with "List deep data charts" and "Get the key driver tree".

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get the deep data entry” operation.

chart.description: Chart shown on the entry card

get.description: Return the key driver tree of the specified stock's performance: each node includes a name, description, importance, child nodes, and linked deep data charts, plus whether drivers exist and the total number of charts. Used by the Key drivers tree on the stock Analysis page and the stock in-depth page.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get the key driver tree” operation.

chart_count.description: Total number of charts linked to drivers

node.description: Root node of the driver tree

get.description: Return all deep data charts of the specified stock (title, description, unit, data series, axis style). Used by the chart list of deep data on the Analysis page. The Broker App can sort them by recent update or data frequency.

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: target_type
parameters.description: Target type; the Broker App passes an empty string

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of items; the Broker App passes `0`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List deep data charts” operation.

get.description: Return one deep data chart by chart ID, used by the driver detail page and chart cards. The chart ID comes from "List deep data charts" or bind_chart.chart_id of a key driver tree node.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Chart ID

parameters.name: max_years
parameters.description: Number of years of data to return; the Broker App detail page passes `20` by default and chart cards pass an empty string

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of data items; the Broker App passes `5` for chart cards and `0` for the detail page

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get a deep data chart” operation.

get.description: Return the operating data charts of the specified stock (one chart per operating indicator), with the same structure as deep data charts. Used by the operating data list on the Analysis page. When a chart is tapped, the Broker App opens the indicator detail by the indicator key of the chart's first series.

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Stock counter_id, such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: target_type
parameters.description: Target type; the Broker App passes an empty string

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List operating data charts” operation.

get.description: Returns the chart for one indicator in the deep-data module on the stock Analysis page, looked up by indicator key: title, unit, data series (bar or line), per-period values with year-over-year and period-over-period changes, and the left and right Y-axis styles. Use it for a deep-data card (pass a small `limit`, such as `5`, to show recent periods) and for the full chart page opened from the card. `key` identifies the deep-data indicator and comes from the deep-data module chart configuration.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), such as `ST/US/AAPL`

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Deep-data indicator key

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of data periods to return. Pass `5` for a card and `0` for the full chart page.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get a Deep-Data Indicator Chart” operation.

get.description: Returns three history series for a market over a date range: market temperature (`temp_list`), valuation (`pe_list`), and sentiment (`up_list`). Use them for the history charts on the market temperature page. Non-trading days in the range have no data points, so the first and last returned dates may differ from the requested range. Hide a series when it is empty. The market temperature page opened from the stock Analysis page uses this endpoint as well.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description:
Market:

- `US` - US stocks
- `HK` - Hong Kong stocks
- `CN` - China A-shares
- `SG` - Singapore

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Start date in `YYYYMMDD` format

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: End date in `YYYYMMDD` format

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Market Temperature History” operation.

get.summary: Get Industry Chains of a Stock
get.description: Returns the industry chains the stock belongs to and their hierarchy: chain, second-level segment, third-level sub-segment, and stocks, with the year-to-date change at each level and where the stock sits in the chain. Use it for the industry chain atlas on the stock Profile page and for the industry chain list page. Pass `items[].id` to Get Industry Chain Stocks and to Get Industry Chain Entity Relations (`type=1`).

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Industry Chains of a Stock” operation.

items.description: Chains. Empty when the stock belongs to none.

get.summary: Get Concept Chains of a Stock
get.description: Returns the concept chains (concept tiers) the stock belongs to and their hierarchy, in the same structure as Get Industry Chains of a Stock. Use it for the concept tier tab of the industry chain atlas on the stock Profile page and for the concept chain list page. Pass `items[].id` to Get Concept Chain Stocks and to Get Industry Chain Entity Relations (`type=2`).

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Concept Chains of a Stock” operation.

items.description: Chains. Empty when the stock belongs to none.

get.summary: List Supply Chain Tabs of a Stock
get.description: Returns the tabs, in order, that the industry chain atlas on the stock Profile page can show. Render tabs in the returned order and hide tabs that are not returned. Each tab gets its data from Get Industry Chains of a Stock, Get Concept Chains of a Stock, Get Supply Chain Relations of a Stock, and related endpoints.

parameters.name: counter_id
parameters.description: Security ID (counter_id), such as `ST/US/AAPL`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List Supply Chain Tabs of a Stock” operation.

list.description:
Tabs to show:

- `industry` - Industry chain
- `concept` - Concept tiers
- `up_down` - Upstream, downstream, and competitors

get.summary: Get Option Chains for Multiple Expirations

Queries option chains for several expiration dates of an underlying stock in one request. Each expiration returns its strike prices, with the call and put contract IDs and extended session support at each strike. Use it to expand several expirations at once on the option chain page. Compared with Get Option-Chain Strike List for a Specified Expiration, it saves one request per expiration. Get expiration dates from the option chain expiration date list. The order page also uses this endpoint to load strikes when the user picks an option contract.

If you use WhaleCore, prefer the corresponding `quoteService()` capability.

- `N` - Non-standard option (adjusted option generated after a corporate action such as a stock split or merger)

Adds one or more securities to the specified watchlist groups of the Client. When `groups` is `[]`, the securities go to the default group. On success, the server updates the watchlist and returns all groups after the change, which the Broker App can use to refresh local state. Used by the **Add to watchlist** button on IPO, signal, and strategy pages. If the request fails, the watchlist is unchanged; the Broker App should roll back any optimistic update and show `message`.

WhaleCore's `watchlistService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `addStocks(counters:groups:removeGroups:sub:)`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

post.description:
Removes one or more securities from the specified watchlist groups of the Client. When `remove_all` is `true`, the securities are removed from every group, which unwatches them. On success, the server updates the watchlist and returns all groups after the change. Used to unwatch securities on IPO, signal, and strategy pages. If the request fails, the watchlist is unchanged; the Broker App should roll back any optimistic update and show `message`.

WhaleCore's `watchlistService()` wraps this endpoint as the typed method `removeStocks(counters:groups:removeAll:)`. If you use WhaleCore, prefer that method.

get.description:
Returns the money market fund (MMF) subscription settings of a Client with an opened account: the subscription mode (automatic or manual selection), and for each currency the available money market funds, the current subscription fund, and whether auto-subscription is paused. The MMF plan page and the subscription management page call it on load to show the current settings and to prepare the data for `POST /portfolio/mmf/save_mmf_purchase`.

`pending_auth_funds` lists funds that were newly added to the fund pool and still need the Client to confirm authorization. A fund that is not in this list is treated as authorized. In automatic mode, show only authorized funds.

For a Client without an opened account, use `GET /ut/mmf/fund/list` to browse the available funds instead.

post.description:
Enables, upgrades, or updates the money market fund (MMF) subscription settings of a Client, including the subscription mode, the subscription fund of each currency, and whether auto-subscription is paused. After a successful save, idle cash is subscribed into money market funds according to the new settings.

Before calling, use `GET /portfolio/mmf/status` to decide the operation: pass `operation` = `2` (update) when `mmf_version` is `1`, otherwise pass `1` (enable or upgrade). `currency_funds` must contain at least one currency entry. To pause or resume auto-subscription for a single currency, submit only that currency entry. In manual mode, each currency can have only one subscription fund.

On failure, handle the business code: guide the Client to complete the CKA when it is missing or expired; otherwise show `message`. A failed save does not change the existing settings, so roll back the changes on the page.

When calling through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

is_auto_purchase.description: Subscription mode: `true` selects the subscription fund automatically; `false` means the Client picks one subscription fund per currency

operation.description:
Operation type:

- `1` - Enable or upgrade MMF
- `2` - Update existing settings

is_paused.description: Whether to pause auto-subscription for this currency

counter_id.description: Security code of the subscription fund. In automatic mode, pass the current subscription fund, or the fund with the highest 7-day annualized yield in this currency when there is none

authorized_counter_ids.description: All fund security codes in this currency that the Client authorizes in automatic mode, submitted in full each time. Required in automatic mode; omit it in manual mode. Omitting it keeps the existing authorization. Do not pass an empty array

400.description: The request failed business rules or input validation. Fix the request based on the business code before retrying.

The Client's CKA has expired. Guide the Client to reassess, then retry

The account has no permission to trade public funds. Show `message` and do not retry
The account is dormant. Show `message` and guide the Client to reactivate the account before retrying
The Client is a restricted Mainland investor and the current IP is in Mainland China. Show `message` and do not retry

post.description:
Returns funds that match filter conditions or a quick filter, used on the fund list (ranking) page and the fund filter page. Advanced and quick filters are mutually exclusive:

- Quick filter: pass an empty `filter` object and set `quick_ids` to the selected `quicks[].id`.
- Advanced filter: pass an empty `quick_ids` array and organize conditions by dimension in `filter`.

The field names of `filter` are the dimension `key` values returned by `GET /v2/funds/options` (such as `fund_attr`, `return`, `risk`, and `cost_performance`). Each value is an object whose field names are indicator `key` values and whose values are arrays. For attribute indicators, pass the selected `options[].key` values: numeric codes (such as `asset_class` and `risk_level`) as integers and others as strings. For metric conditions, pass both the period leaf (such as `return_rate_period`) and the value leaf (`[min, max]` for a range, `[value]` for a single value). When neither mode carries any condition, all funds are returned.

Parse list items as `FundB30Summary`; `earning_rate` covers the period in `time_interval`. This operation is read-only.

post.description:
Checks whether the account-opening ID number entered by the Client matches the account-opening records under the specified Broker channel. It is the identity verification step in flows such as setting or resetting the trade password. Common flows:

- Reset trade password (`scene` = `3`): after verification, send a code to the Client’s contact phone and verify it, then call `POST /v2/member/trade/reset_password` to set the new password.
- Set trade password (`scene` = `4`): after verification, send a code to the Client’s contact phone and verify it, then set the trade password.

Pass the Broker channel where the Client opened the account in `account_channel`. If verification fails, show `message` and let the Client re-enter the number; if the Client repeatedly fails, direct them to customer service.

Never send `card_id` in plaintext. Encryption: compute the MD5 of the `x-timestamp` header value (a millisecond timestamp string) as a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal string. Use the UTF-8 bytes of that string as the AES key and its first 16 bytes as the IV, encrypt the plaintext with AES-CBC (PKCS#7 padding), and Base64-encode the ciphertext as `k`. Then Base64-encode the JSON string `{"rd":"<x-timestamp>","k":"<k>"}` and send it as the field value. `rd` must match the `x-timestamp` header, which the server uses for decryption.

parameters.name: x-timestamp
parameters.description: Millisecond timestamp string; must match `rd` in the encrypted field

card_id.description: Encrypted account-opening ID number; see the operation description for the encryption method

- `3` - Reset trade password
- `4` - Set trade password

Checks whether the Client's risk assessment result meets the fund risk level. This is the first step of the fund order flow and does not create an order. The recommended order flow is:

1. Make sure the trade token is valid.
2. Call this endpoint and handle `user_pi`: continue on `2`; on `0` or `3`, guide the Client to open `eval_address` to complete or redo the risk assessment; on `1`, show `user_risk_level` and `fund_risk_level` and explain the mismatch. Do not continue unless the value is `2`.
3. Call Get Fund Order Certification Checks and stop if any item has `is_force` set to `true`.
4. After the Client confirms, call Submit Fund Order with the `auth_token` returned here.

Also used to check the risk level before creating or modifying a recurring investment plan.

post.description:
Submits a fund buy (subscription) or sell (redemption) order. On success, the order is created and the Client's available cash (buy) or sellable units (sell) change accordingly, so refresh the asset and holdings display. The order is then confirmed with NAV and units according to the fund dealing date, and you can track it with Get Fund Order Details. When the order `withdrawable` is `true`, it can be canceled.

Prerequisites: the trade token is valid; for a buy, Validate Fund Order Risk (`user_pi` is `2`) and Get Fund Order Certification Checks (no `is_force` item) have been completed in order; and the Client has accepted the fund documents and agreement. For a buy, pass `amount` and `dividend_option`. For a sell, pass `units`, and set `is_sell_all` to `true` to sell the entire holding.

On failure, no order is created. Handle compliance business codes as described and show `message` to the Client for other errors. Whether the service deduplicates repeated submissions is not confirmed. If the request times out, check Get Fund Order List for a new order before deciding whether to submit again.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

post.summary: Create or Modify Recurring Investment Plan
post.description:
Creates a recurring investment plan when `plan_id` is omitted, or modifies the cycle, debit day, and amount per installment of the plan when it is passed. On success, the plan debits automatically on the chosen cycle and creates one fund buy order per installment. When creating a plan, setting `invest_now` to `true` invests the first installment immediately and uses the corresponding cash.

Prerequisites: the trade token is valid; Get Fund Tradable Types has confirmed `is_allow_aip` is `true`; Validate Fund Order Risk (`user_pi` is `2`) and Get Fund Order Certification Checks (no `is_force` item) have been completed; the amount per installment is not below the minimum subscription amount and, when investing immediately, does not exceed `limit_amount` from Get Fund Purchasing Power; and the Client has accepted the recurring investment agreement. You can call Calculate Next Recurring Investment Debit Time first to show the first debit date.

On failure, the plan is not created or modified. Handle compliance business codes as described and show `message` to the Client for other errors. Whether the service deduplicates repeated submissions is not confirmed. Prevent repeated taps, and after a timeout, check Get My Recurring Investment Plans before retrying.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

cycle.description:
Investment cycle:

- `1` - Daily
- `2` - Weekly
- `3` - Every two weeks
- `4` - Monthly

cycle_day.description: Debit day: `1`-`5` (Monday to Friday) for weekly and biweekly cycles; `1`-`31` for monthly, where `32` means the last day of the month. Not used for the daily cycle

invest_amount.description: Amount per installment in the fund settlement currency

invest_now.description: Whether to invest the first installment immediately when creating. Pass `false` when modifying

post.description:
Pauses, resumes, or ends a recurring investment plan. After a pause, no further debits are made; after a resume, debits continue on the original cycle. Ending a plan cannot be undone, and the plan no longer runs. Ask the Client to confirm again before pausing or ending. On success, call Get Recurring Investment Plan Details again to refresh the state. Orders already created are not affected. On failure, the plan keeps its state. Handle compliance business codes as described and show `message` to the Client for other errors.

When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

post.description:
Turns the Client's SMS two-factor verification on or off. It maps to the SMS verification item in the two-factor verification settings. Choose `action` from the Client's current state: pass `close` if it is on, or `open` if it is off.

Before calling, send an SMS verification code to the Client's bound mobile number (the send-code operation is outside the scope of this document), then put the code the Client enters in `code`. On success the setting changes immediately, so fetch the Client settings again to refresh the toggle. On failure, show `message` and let the Client request or enter a new code.

For the SMS second-factor step during trade unlock, see Submit SMS Verification for Trade Unlock.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

Target state:

- `open` - Turn on SMS two-factor verification
- `close` - Turn off SMS two-factor verification

code.description: SMS verification code received by the Client. Required when verification is completed with an SMS code

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Toggle SMS Two-Factor Verification” operation.

get.description:
Gets the QR code content and secret the Client needs to bind a third-party authenticator (a TOTP app such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator). The Broker App renders `qr_code_url` as a QR code for the Client to scan and shows `secret` for manual entry.

Binding flow: the Client first completes SMS verification of the bound mobile number, then the Broker App calls this operation to show the QR code. After adding the account in the authenticator, the Client submits a code it generates through Set Authenticator Two-Factor Verification to finish turning it on.

If the Client has already bound an authenticator, business code `402017` is returned. Show `message` and end the binding flow.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Authenticator Binding QR Code” operation.

qr_code_url.description: QR code content. The Broker App encodes this string into a QR code as is

secret.description: Authenticator secret for manual entry when the Client cannot scan the QR code

400.description: The service rejected the request because a business rule or input validation failed. Review the business codes and correct the request before retrying.

x-business-codes.description: The Client has already bound an authenticator. The Broker App shows `message` and ends the binding flow

post.description:
Turns the Client's third-party authenticator (TOTP) two-factor verification on or off. Once it is on, verifying the trade password during trade unlock may return `need_totp_two_factors: true`; then call Submit Authenticator Code for Trade Unlock.

- To turn it on: pass `YES` in `totp_2fa_auth` and the code currently shown in the Client's authenticator in `verify_code` to confirm the binding.
- To turn it off: pass `NO` in `totp_2fa_auth`. `verify_code` is not needed.

Both actions require the Client to pass SMS verification of the bound mobile number first. Put the credential returned by that check in `verify_credentials` (the check operation is outside the scope of this document). If the credential has expired, business code `403046` is returned; in the turn-on flow, have the Client complete SMS verification again. If the code is wrong, show `message` and let the Client enter it again. On success, refresh the two-factor verification settings shown to the Client.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

totp_2fa_auth.description:
Target state:

- `YES` - Turn on authenticator two-factor verification
- `NO` - Turn off authenticator two-factor verification

verify_credentials.description: Verification credential obtained after the SMS code check passes. It expires after a period of time

verify_code.description: Current 6-digit code shown in the authenticator. Required when `totp_2fa_auth` is `YES`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Set Authenticator Two-Factor Verification” operation.

400.description: The service rejected the request because a business rule or input validation failed. Review the business codes and correct the request before retrying.

get.description:
Checks whether the signed-in Client has user agreement updates to confirm again, and returns the copy for the update prompt and the agreement links. The Broker App calls it after the Client signs in. When `hit` is `true`, show the `windows.main` dialog and render text in `text_main` that matches `highlights[].name` as links to `highlights[].url`. When `hit` is `false`, no dialog is needed.

- If the Client agrees, call Record Accepted Agreement Versions with the `key` and `version` of every agreement in `highlights`.
- If the Client declines, show the `windows.cancel` confirmation dialog. Sign the Client out if they confirm; show `windows.main` again if they go back.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

If the request fails, submit again at the next agreement update check.

Each item in `agreements_info` carries the agreement key, version, and signed flag. On success, close the agreement page and notify the App that the agreement is signed; on failure, show `message` and let the Client submit again.

This operation is used by both the mandatory account agreement page and the risk agreement signing page.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

get.description:
Gets the Securities Borrowing and Lending Agreement (SBLA) signing state of the current account. The agreement must be signed before short selling Hong Kong stocks. The Broker App calls it when the agreement page opens. When `state` is `0` and `blacklist_state` is empty, show the full agreement for the Client to sign; otherwise show the result according to `state` and `blacklist_state`.

When `state` is `0`, `3`, or `5` and `blacklist_state` is returned, use `blacklist_state` to explain why the Client cannot sign.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target funding account. The H5 page passes the current account; if omitted, the current account of the session is used

parameters.description: Account channel (account_channel) of the current account. The H5 page passes it when available

state.description:
Signing state:

- `0` - Not signed
- `1` - Signed; the Client can trade Hong Kong stocks on short selling
- `2` - Under review; related fees may be frozen in the account during signing
- `3` - Deduction failed; the account does not have enough quota or assets to freeze or deduct the fee. The Client must reserve enough funds and sign again
- `4` - Signing failed; the Client must sign again
- `5` - Invalidated; see `reason`. The Client must sign again

blacklist_state.description:
Reason the Client cannot sign. It may be empty:

- `1` - The Client cannot short sell Hong Kong stocks for now. Direct the Client to customer service
- `2` - The Client has no financing quota and must apply for a quota before signing again

Submits the Client's Securities Borrowing and Lending Agreement (SBLA) signing. After the Client reads the agreement and taps Sign, call Get Account Opening E-Signature first. If it returns `key`, submit it directly as `signature_key`; otherwise have the Client draw a signature, upload the image, and submit the returned file key (the upload operation is outside the scope of this document).

A successful submission only means the signing request was accepted. The final result is the `state` returned by Get SBLA Signing State. Whether the submission succeeds or fails, query the state again and refresh the page; on failure, show `message`. Processing may take a while, so set a longer timeout for this request (for example, 30 seconds).

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

version.description: Version of the signed agreement, provided by the agreement entry point

An empty `list`, or fewer items than `page_size`, means there are no more messages.

Reading messages does not change their read status. To clear the group's unread messages, call `DELETE /v6/message/inbox/clear_unreads`.

The price alert history page also uses this operation to read the alert message group and show triggered price alerts.

- Mark a group as read: pass `group_id` and `status=1` without `ids` to mark every message in the group as read. Call it when the Client opens a group.

After success, call `GET /v6/message/inbox/unreads_count` and `GET /v6/message/inbox/groups/summary` again to refresh the badge and the per-group unread counts. On failure, keep the local unread state and do not clear the badge in advance.

- Code 2100004: the Client has not completed accredited investor certification. Handle it the same way.
- Other failures: show `message`.
- Success with a non-empty `validate_list`: show the `message` of the first item and close the detail page after the Client acknowledges it.

After this check passes, call `GET /v1/wms/orders/check` when the Client taps Buy.

Call it when the Client taps Buy on the product detail page. It checks whether the Client and product meet the order conditions: product status, account status, risk level match, derivatives knowledge assessment, and risk assessment validity. It only checks and creates no order. Handle the result in this order:

1. `error_type` is `4`: the Client has not completed the derivatives knowledge assessment. Let the Client complete it, record the result through `POST /v1/record/questionnaire` with `type` set to `derivatives.HK`, then call this operation again.
2. `error_type` is `7`: the risk assessment has expired. Show `message` and guide the Client to reassess.
3. `error_type` is `3`: the risk level does not match. An empty `risk_level` means the Client has not completed a risk assessment. Show `message` and guide the Client to take or retake the assessment.
4. Any other non-empty `validate_list`: show `message` and block the order.
5. Empty `validate_list`: the check passed. If the product is a complex product (`complex_product=1` from `GET /v2/wms/product/detail`), let the Client confirm the complex product declaration first, then open the order page and call `GET /v1/wms/orders/data_info`.

If the request fails, show `message` and do not open the order page.

get.description:
Call it when the order page opens. It returns the account's available funds and financing information in the product currency, product elements, selectable price types, and documents. This operation is read-only.

Validate the subscription amount `quantity` on the order page as follows:

- It must be a positive multiple of `product_details.denomination` and cannot be 0.
- Amount payable = `quantity` × `product_details.client_price`.
- When `cash_info.support_financing` is `1`, the amount payable cannot exceed `cash_info.buy_on_margin`. Otherwise it cannot exceed `cash_info.withdraw`.
- When financing is supported and the amount payable exceeds `cash_info.withdraw`, the excess is financed. Set `pay_mode` to `1` when submitting, and you can call `POST /v1/wms/orders/get_finance_info` to estimate the interest.

When `product_details.order_price_types` is not empty, the Client must choose a price type for each underlying. With multiple underlyings, call `POST /v1/wms/orders/additional-price-types` to get the price types that remain selectable.

- Request failure: show `message` and let the Client decide whether to submit again.

Activates a strategy risk level for the client after the client confirms the risk disclosure of that level. Once activated, the client can view strategies, signals, and other content restricted to that level (`R1`–`R5`); for levels that are not activated, the content stays locked or has fields removed.

The server rejects requests that fail compliance rules, for example when the risk assessment has expired or the selected level is above the client's risk tolerance; show the `message` in the response to the client. A successful response does not return the updated set of activated levels; query the client's activated levels again to confirm the result (that query endpoint is outside the scope of this document), and refresh content that depends on the levels.

get.description:
Returns the Client current risk assessment level and Professional Investor (PI) certification status. The Broker App calls it before opening the risk assessment page or the PI certification page. If `risk` has a value, show the existing assessment result directly. If `pi` is `1` (under review) or `3` (certified), do not start the certification flow again.

When `pi` is `3`, also check `re_authentication` and `pi_end_at` to decide whether recertification is needed. `pending` means a recertification has already been submitted, so do not prompt again. `un_pass` means the recertification was rejected, so guide the Client to submit again. If there is no recertification record and `pi_end_at` is approaching, tell the Client that the certification is about to expire.

After a risk assessment or PI certification is submitted, the server updates the status with a delay, so an immediate query may still return the previous status. This operation is also used to check the risk level and PI eligibility before fund trading and IPO subscriptions.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Risk Assessment and Professional Investor Status” operation.

pi.description:
Professional Investor certification status:
- `0` - Not submitted
- `1` - Under review
- `2` - Failed
- `3` - Certified

risk.description: Risk assessment level. `A1` to `A5` correspond to conservative, moderate, balanced, growth, and aggressive. Empty means the Client has not completed the assessment.

pi_end_at.description: Expiry time of the PI certification as a Unix timestamp in seconds

re_authentication.description:
Recertification status:
- `pending` - Recertification under review
- `un_pass` - Recertification rejected
- Empty string - No recertification record

post.description:
Submits the Client risk tolerance assessment answers. The server calculates the risk level from the assessment configuration and returns it. Questions, options, and scores come from the server-side assessment configuration (configuration ID `risk_account_application`). The Broker App renders the questions from that configuration and adds each selected value to `content` as a `{key, value}` item. For multiple-choice questions, join the values with commas.

Side effect: after a successful submission, the Client risk level becomes the returned `risk`, and `GET /v1/member/ut/states` returns the new level afterwards, possibly with a short delay. If the Client already has a result and wants to retake the assessment, call `GET /v1/member/ut/check_frequency_limit` first. If the submission fails, show `message` and do not change the level already shown.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

key.description: Question number, such as `Q1`

value.description: Selected option value, such as `A`. For multiple-choice questions, join values with commas, such as `A,B`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Risk Assessment” operation.

risk.description: Risk level after the assessment, from `A1` to `A5`

get.description:
Checks whether the Client can retake the risk assessment now. The Broker App calls it when a Client who already has a result chooses to retake the assessment. A successful request means the Client can retake it; ask the Client to confirm and then clear the previous answers. Business code `404423` means the retake limit has been reached; tell the Client and stop the retake. You do not need to parse `data` on success.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: scene
parameters.description: Assessment scene. Use the same `scene` as when submitting the assessment; pass `mmf`.

parameters.name: account_channel
parameters.description: Broker channel

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Risk Assessment Retake Limit” operation.

400.description: The request failed business rules or input validation. Fix the request based on the business code before retrying.

x-business-codes.description: The risk assessment retake limit has been reached

post.description:
Submits the Client Professional Investor (PI) certification application for review. Prerequisites: the Client has read the PI declaration, agreed to it, and signed with their full name. `signature` must match the English name on the Client account (for a joint account, “primary holder English name/joint holder English name”); the Broker App should check this before submitting. Upload proof-of-asset files (PDF or images) through `GET /v1/file/upload_url` first and put the file keys in `poas`. If the Client assets meet the certification threshold, no proof is needed and `poas` can be an empty array.

Side effect: after a successful submission, the application goes to review and `pi` in `GET /v1/member/ut/states` becomes `1` (under review). The status updates with a delay, so query it again later. If the submission fails, show `message` and keep the uploaded files so the Client can retry. This operation is also used for PI certification during account opening.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

poas.description: File keys of the proof-of-asset files. Can be an empty array when the assets meet the certification threshold.

signature.description: Full name signed by the Client. Must match the English name on the account.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Professional Investor Certification” operation.

post.description:
Records that the Client has read and agreed to the fund risk disclosure, and enables fund trading for the Client. The Broker App shows the disclosure page when the Client buys or sells a fund for the first time and must confirm the disclosure first. After the Client confirms, complete trade password verification and then call this operation.

Side effect: on success, the Client can trade funds, and the Broker App closes the disclosure page and opens the fund order page. If it fails, show `message` and do not open the order page.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Confirm Fund Risk Disclosure” operation.

post.description:
Checks in one request whether the Client has completed the specified risk declarations or knowledge questionnaires. On the options trading permission page, the Broker App passes the identifier of each prerequisite task (such as `flag.options` or `flag.optionsquestionnaire`) and marks each task as completed or not based on the result. Query again when the Client returns from a task page.

Each value is either completed (`true`) or not completed (`false`). There is no under-review state.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

keys.description: Identifiers of the declarations or questionnaires to check, such as `flag.options`, `flag.optionsquestionnaire`, `flag.warrant`, and `flag.otc`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Check Declaration and Questionnaire Completion” operation.

data.description: Keyed by the identifiers in the request. Each value indicates whether the item is completed.

post.description:
Returns the compliance questionnaires and declarations that the Client still needs to fill in or sign. The Broker App calls it in two cases:

- Before opening a questionnaire page, check by `info.questionnaire_id` that the questionnaire is still in the list. If it is not, it has already been submitted, so go to the result page.
- After a questionnaire is submitted, take the items that have `fronts.btn_agree.url`, sort them by `info.priority` in ascending order, and guide the Client to the first one.

If the query fails, do not stop the Client from filling in the current questionnaire.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “List Pending Questionnaires” operation.

main.title: Complete the customer due diligence questionnaire
main.content: To keep your account secure, update your information.

get.description:
Exchanges the `token` in a questionnaire link for questionnaire information and decides which page the Client opens. Compliance questionnaires such as customer due diligence are sent to the Client as links that carry a `token`. When the Broker App opens such a link, it calls this operation first and handles the result in this order:

1. If `questionnaire_state` is `2`, `3`, `4`, or `5` (final states), go to the result page.
2. If `unavailable` or `questionnaire_unavailable` is `true`, show that the questionnaire is unavailable.
3. If `required` is `false`, go to the result page.
4. If `template_source` is `custom`, the server provides the questions; call `GET /v1/kyc/questionnaire/token_exchange_questions` to get them.
5. Otherwise, it is a predefined template questionnaire and `code` identifies its type. If `template_source` is `hardcoded`, also confirm through `POST /v1/account/get_popup_list` that it is still pending.

Use the returned `token` in later requests; if none is returned, keep using the `token` from the link. If the request fails, tell the Client and allow a retry; do not treat it as an unavailable questionnaire.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: `token` from the questionnaire link

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Resolve Questionnaire Link” operation.

questionnaire_state.description:
Questionnaire state:
- `0` - No questionnaire record
- `1` - Pending signature
- `2` - Signing failed
- `3` - Signed
- `4` - Pending review
- `5` - Withdrawn

unavailable.description: Whether the questionnaire entry is unavailable

questionnaire_unavailable.description: Whether the questionnaire is unavailable. Same meaning as `unavailable`; if either is `true`, it is unavailable.

required.description: Whether the Client needs to fill it in. `false` means no. Treat a missing value as required.

token.description: Questionnaire token to use in later requests

code.description: Type identifier of a predefined template questionnaire

template_source.description:
Question source:
- `custom` - Questions provided by the server
- `hardcoded` - Predefined template

questionnaire_id.description: Questionnaire ID used when submitting. If it is not returned, use `template_id`.

get.description:
Gets the questions provided by the server for a questionnaire `token`. The Broker App uses it to render dynamic questionnaires whose `template_source` is `custom`, and on the result page to match and show submitted answers.

Only items whose `type` is `question` are questions. `question.content` and `question.options` are JSON strings that must be parsed again. Questions whose `is_kyc_field` is `true` can be prefilled from the Client KYC profile. When options come from a remote data source, fetch them separately by `ref`. If the request fails, tell the Client and allow a retry; do not show an empty questionnaire.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: `token` from the questionnaire link

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Questionnaire Questions” operation.

Returns the answers last submitted for the questionnaire so that the result page can show what the Client submitted. Match `answers[].key` against the question `field_key` first. If there is no match, compare it with every language version of the question text, because non-KYC fields are submitted with the question text as the key, in the language used at submission. Do not show answers that match neither. If the query fails, you can skip showing the submitted answers.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: `token` from the questionnaire link

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Last Submitted Questionnaire Answers” operation.

post.description:
Submits a compliance questionnaire filled in by the Client, creates a review ticket, and returns `ticket_id`. Prerequisites: `questionnaire_id` has been obtained through `GET /v1/kyc/questionnaire/code_exchange`. For dynamic questionnaires, show the important notice before submission and have the Client confirm it.

Answers take one of two forms, depending on the questionnaire: the `answers` array (used by dynamic questionnaires and most others) or the `answer` map. If there are upload questions, upload the files first to get their keys, put the keys in the `value` of the answer (comma-separated for multiple files), and list all file keys in `attachments.keys`.

Side effect: a successful submission creates a review ticket. You can then call `POST /v1/account/get_popup_list` to guide the Client to the next questionnaire. If the submission fails, show `message` and keep what the Client entered so they can retry.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: AAID of the target account. When the Client has several accounts under the same tenant, it specifies which account the questionnaire belongs to.

answers.description: Answers in array form. Use either this or `answer`. Leave out questions with empty values.

key.description: For KYC fields, the `field_key`. For other fields, the question text in the current language.

value.description: Answer. For non-KYC choice questions, the option text; for KYC fields, the raw value. Join multiple selections with commas. For upload questions, comma-separated file keys.

service.description: Storage service for upload questions. Pass `user.account`.

type.description:
Answer type:
- `image` - Image upload
- `file` - File upload
- `ref` - KYC field whose options come from a remote data source

answer.description: Answers in map form, keyed by question identifier. Use either this or `answers`.

attachments.description: Attachments. Pass only when files were uploaded.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit Compliance Questionnaire” operation.

After `GET /v2/questionnaire/has` reports a questionnaire, the Broker App calls this operation with the matched scene as `position`, shows the questions one by one, and submits the answers through `POST /v1/questionnaire/submit`.

If a question has `relation`, show it only after the question it depends on has one of the specified options selected. If the request fails, tell the Client and allow a retry; do not show an empty questionnaire. This operation is also used for the survey after a stock transfer-out.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

`data` is keyed by certification type, such as `w8` (Form W-8BEN), `cka`, and `car`. `cka` and `car` are usually shown together as one entry. The returned types depend on the Client, so the Broker App should not assume a fixed set of keys.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

The Broker App shows it together with the account opening information on the W-8BEN confirmation page so that the Client can review it and confirm through `PUT /v1/account/confirm_w8beninfo`. If the request fails, show `message`.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, you do not need to set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

The Broker App shows the Client account opening information and the country from `GET /v1/account/w8_country` on the W-8BEN confirmation page, and calls this operation after the Client reviews it and confirms again.

Side effect: confirms the W-8BEN information with the current details; on success, go to the result page. If any information is incorrect, do not call this operation; guide the Client to contact customer service instead. If it fails, show `message`.

Requests an account opening proof, a proof of assets, or a no-trading proof for the Client. On the proof request page, the Broker App collects the proof type, languages, and other details, confirms the receiving email address (the Client bound email) with the Client, completes trade password verification, and then calls this operation.

Pass fields based on `apply.type`: a proof of assets needs `account_no`; a no-trading proof needs `account_no`, `start_date`, and `end_date`.

Side effect: submits the request; on success, go to the request result page. If it fails, show `message`.

When you call this operation through WhaleCore `requestService()`, set `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

Proof type:
- `1` - Account opening proof
- `2` - Proof of assets
- `3` - No-trading proof

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Request Account Proof Document” operation.

get.description:
Checks, when the Client opens the account closure page, whether the target account meets the closure conditions, so that the page can list each item the Client must resolve first. A value of `true` in any of the following fields means that the corresponding condition is not met; do not let the Client submit the closure in that case:

- Positions or a cash balance remain (`has_assets_remaining`)
- Dividends or corporate actions are still pending (`frozen_interest.has_interest_amount`, `frozen_interest.has_corp_action`)
- Trades or asset changes occurred today (`has_assets_changed`)
- Bank cards are still linked (`has_bank_card_bound`)

After all conditions are met, verify the Client's identity first (for example, with an SMS or email verification code), and then call `POST /v1/account/close_account` to submit the closure.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the target account. The operation checks the closure conditions for this account.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Query Account Closure Conditions” operation.

post.description: Submits a closure request for the current account. This action cannot be undone, so ask the Client to confirm before submitting. - Live account: call `GET /v1/account/close_account_validate` first to confirm that all closure conditions are met, and verify the Client's identity (for example, with an SMS or email verification code) before calling this endpoint. Pass the account to close in the `x-target-aaid` header. A successful response only means that the closure request was accepted. The closure is processed in the background, and the Client is notified when it is complete. - Demo account: use this endpoint to reset demo assets. Closing the demo account clears its asset information, and the Client can open a new demo account later. Refresh the account list after success. If the request fails, show `message` to the Client. For a live account, identity verification codes can be used only once, so do not verify an already accepted code again when retrying the submission. Closing a live account requires a trade token. When you call this endpoint through WhaleCore `requestService()` for a live account, declare the trade token requirement by setting `requiresTradeToken` to `true`.

parameters.name: x-target-aaid
parameters.description: The `aaid` of the account to close.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Close Account” operation.

get.description:
Retrieves the progress of the reactivation flow for the current account after it becomes dormant because of long inactivity, so that the reactivation page can decide which step to show. Three status fields drive the flow, each taking `0` (step not required), `1` (not submitted), `2` (under review), or `3` (review completed):

- If `update_apl_ticket_status` is `2`, an update to the account opening information is under review. Wait until it is approved before submitting the reactivation.
- If both `activate_ticket_status` and `questionnaire_status` are `3`, the account is already active and no submission is needed.
- If the reactivation has been submitted and `questionnaire_status` is `1`, direct the Client to `questionnaire_link` to complete the questionnaire.
- In other not-yet-submitted states, after the Client confirms that the account opening information needs no changes, call `POST /v1/member/account/activate_dormant_account` to submit the reactivation.

Call this endpoint again after the reactivation or questionnaire is submitted to refresh the progress.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Dormant Account Reactivation Info” operation.

post.description:
Submits a reactivation request for the current dormant account after the Client confirms that the account opening information is up to date and needs no changes. Send an empty object as the request body.

Call `GET /v1/member/account/get_activate_dormant_info` before submitting. Do not submit while an account opening information update is under review (`update_apl_ticket_status` is `2`) or when the account is already active. A successful response only means that the reactivation request was accepted. The review runs in the background, and the Client is notified of the result by email and in-app notification. After success, call `GET /v1/member/account/get_activate_dormant_info` again: if `questionnaire_status` is `1`, direct the Client to `questionnaire_link` to complete the questionnaire; otherwise, show the under-review state.

If the request fails, tell the Client that the submission failed and to try again later.

schema.description: Reactivation request. No fields are currently required; send an empty object `{}`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Reactivate Dormant Account” operation.

Claims an unclaimed e-voucher (`deliver_status` is `0`). The request body is form-encoded.

- `status` is `0`: Accepted but not complete; for example, a voucher can take several business days to arrive. Query the e-voucher list or prize details again later to confirm.

The prize details page also uses this endpoint to claim e-vouchers that require contact details; in that case pass the Client's contact details in `extra`. On failure, show `message`.

Returns a single prize (physical goods, e-voucher, or redemption code) by reward record ID, for the prize details page that shows the item, grant and delivery status, fulfillment and recipient details, e-voucher claim result, and whether it can be exchanged for a cash card. Fields match the `prize` object in `GET /rewards/member_reward_list`.

For physical goods, `deliver_status` can also return `8` (address not provided), `9` or `11` (address provided), or `10` (shipping). Decide the next step from `status` and `deliver_status`:

- Before a tracking number `deliver_order` exists, call `POST /rewards/update_express_info` to provide or change recipient details.
- When `to_cash_card` is `true`, call `POST /reward/prize/to/cash-card` to exchange it for a cash card.

parameters.name: record_id
parameters.description: Prize record ID, that is, `prize.record_id`

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get prize details” operation.

post.description:
Submits or changes the fulfillment method and recipient details for a physical prize: for shipping, submit the recipient, phone, and address; for pickup, submit a contact email and pickup location. Available methods and pickup locations are `delivery_types` and `addresses` from `GET /rewards/reward_prize_info`.

You can submit when either condition is met:

- `status` is `8` or `10`, and `deliver_status` is `0` or `8`.
- `status` is `8` or `12`, no tracking number `deliver_order` exists, and `deliver_status` is `0`, `8`, `9`, or `11`.

Once a tracking number is generated, the address is locked and cannot be changed. After success, call `GET /rewards/reward_prize_info` again to refresh the status. On failure, show `message`.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Submit prize recipient details” operation.

get.description: Returns the recipient details the Client submitted the last time they claimed a physical prize, for prefilling the recipient form.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get last-used recipient details” operation.

post.description: Call this when the Client chooses a cash card instead of the physical prize; applies to prizes where `to_cash_card` is `true`. After success, the reward status becomes exchanged (`16`) and the physical prize can no longer be claimed. On failure, show `message`.

When `state` is `unchoiced`, call `POST /v1/activity/rewards/choice_reward_group` to submit a choice.

The choice cannot be changed after submission. After success, the rewards are being granted; call `GET /v1/activity/rewards/reward_groups` again to refresh the state. On failure, show `message`.

get.description:
Call this endpoint when the order page loads. It returns the dates that can be selected as the good-till-date (GTD) expiry for orders in the given market. When the Client chooses "good till date" for a limit order, conditional order, grid trading order, or take-profit/stop-loss order, the Broker App renders the expiry date picker from this list and submits the selected date as the order expiry date.

The Broker enables this capability in tenant configuration. If it is not enabled or the list is empty, the Broker App uses its own date picker and limits the selectable range according to the order configuration (the time-in-force support returned by `GET /v5/orders/info`).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market code of the security, such as `HK` or `US`. It matches the market segment of the security counter_id.

200.description: The request succeeded. The response body contains the result of the “Get Available Order Expiry Dates” operation.

date.description: Selectable expiry dates in `yyyy-MM-dd` format, in ascending order.
